title: the WSG fatigue chapter slice - the close-to-the-ground dismount tail closing the wilderness combat chapter and the full fatigue and exhaustion rules for characters, land-based mounts and flying mounts, printed pp. 87-89, CLOSING the wilderness combat chapter and the fatigue chapter
audit_label: R489 WSG fatigue chapter pin audit
audit_comment: The fatigue and exhaustion chapter with the p. 87 dismount tail: the close-to-the-ground flying-mount death allowing the proficient rider to leap and land safely, closing the wilderness combat chapter. Characters: strenuous activity past 4 turns risks fatigue (over-full movement, melee, continuous climbing, swimming against a strong current, severe encumbrance), 2 consecutive turns of rest avoid the risk, the first Constitution Check at 6 turns, success buying 5 more turns with the interval shrinking by 1 to a minimum of 1; fatigue drops every ability score except comeliness by 2 until 2 consecutive hours of rest, with the 18-strength, 18-constitution and 14-wisdom examples (lost to-hit and reduced damage, 2 hit points per hit die at a temporary 16, and both bonus 1st-level spells lost with a spell-failure chance at an effective 12); checks read the current score, a further -2 on attacks and saves, a per-turn Constitution Check while continuing, failure meaning exhaustion with another -2 and no voluntary action except when failure to move risks death; 1 hour of rest plus a successful check leaves only fatigue, cleared by 2 more hours; rest while carried when no strength or balance is needed and no jostling occurs, and rest tied to a mount moving easily over easy ground. Land-based mounts: 2 days without food and water or 3 days short rations fatigues, full ration plus 8 hours rest recovers, overwork recovery is 12 hours plus 2 per hour overworked (the 3-hour horse resting 18); the fatigued animal moves at half rate with 1-round-per-turn bursts, cannot negotiate 3-inch terrain (the loaded horse and the camel in very rugged ground), and is 2 armor class places worse (7 to 9); only an animal-handling proficient character can calm the excited fatigued animal and only at the nonproficient chance; forced work risks a cumulative 20 percent exhaustion chance per hour, reset by an hour of rest; the exhausted animal stops in its tracks, may collapse (25 unburdened, 50 burdened, 75 overloaded), is oblivious, will not panic and will not defend itself, faces a flat 50 percent death chance within 1d4 hours, and drains 1d6 minus 3 hit points per hour through an 8-hour critical period, regaining 2 per hour after survival but still fatigued. Flying mounts: never exhausted; the stamina table first number is safe flying time (reduced when heavily loaded), past it a 1d10 per turn with the fatigue chance 10 minus the rest number (the black dragon 24/6 fatiguing on 1-4); flying and rest need not be full blocks (the 30-turn window with 24 aloft and 6 rest, the 7-turn last flight risking fatigue), exceeding the safe time then landing demands a full rest period; on fatigue the rate drops to two-thirds with 10 yards of altitude lost per round, a same-turn safe landing within 100 yards, past that a second-turn steep dive with 1d2 buffet damage per 10 yards dived halved for airborne-riding proficiency or secure strapping, the unstrapped rider thrown for 11-40 (3d10 plus 10); after landing the mount refuses flight for three times its rest period (18 turns for the dragon) unless self-preservation dictates otherwise, early takeoff risking fatigue every turn aloft.

banner.title: R489: the WSG FATIGUE chapter slice, printed pp. 87-89 - the round CLOSING the wilderness combat chapter with the close-to-the-ground dismount tail and landing the FULL fatigue and exhaustion chapter: the character strenuous rhythm with the shrinking check intervals and the fatigue and exhaustion penalties with their recovery chains and the carried-rest rules, the land-based mount nourishment and overwork rules with the fatigued movement and armor class effects and the cumulative exhaustion chance with the collapse ladder and the trauma drain, and the flying-mount stamina rules with the 1d10 fatigue check and the steep-dive buffet and thrown-rider damage - the mounts and beasts of burden catalog rides to R490.
banner.provenance: THE SETTLE: two-way clean on the first pass - the tesseract full-text reads, the pdftotext layout read and the tsv coordinate reads agree on every number (the 4-turn risk, the 2-turn rest, the 6-turn check, the 5 more turns, the 1-turn step and minimum, the score drop of 2 with the 2-hour clear, the example scores 18 18 and 14 with the temporary 16 and effective 12, the per-turn check, the 1-hour exhausted recovery, the 2 and 3 day animal nutrition bars with the 8-hour rest, the 12-plus-2 overwork formula with the 18-hour horse example, the half rate with the 1-round bursts, the 3-inch terrain bar, the 7-to-9 armor class example, the 20 percent cumulative chance with the 1-hour reset, the 25 50 75 collapse ladder, the flat 50 percent death chance within 1d4 hours, the 1d6-minus-3 trauma drain through 8 hours with the 2-per-hour regain, the 24/6 black dragon with the 1-4 on 1d10, the 30-turn non-block window, the two-thirds rate with 10 yards per round, the 100-yard same-turn landing bar, the 1d2 buffet per 10 yards, the 11-40 thrown damage as 3d10 plus 10, and the three-times 18-turn post-fatigue rest). The garbles settled without contest: the layout l d 4 l d 6 l d l O l d 2 and 1dlO classes are 1d4 1d6 1d10 and 1d2, Constutition and conscutive are the book typos for constitution and consecutive, 3 inches renders the 3-inch terrain bar, and hump(s) survives the hump-at glyph. The p. 87 cut turned out to be a column wrap WITHIN the page, not a page cut: the right column carries the Dungeon Master may allow a character with proficiency in riding the mount to leap from its back and land safely on the ground - the dismount section is complete and only the connective pin rides to this round.
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: the fatigue score drop equals the exhausted extra drop equals the attack and save penalty, the shrinking check interval floors at the step size, the animal nutrition bars run 2 and 3 days with the 8-hour recovery, the overwork formula makes the 3-hour horse rest 18, the fatigued animal moves at half rate with the 3-inch bar and the two-place armor class example, the collapse ladder climbs 25 50 75 in equal steps, the trauma roll floors at zero with the 8-hour critical period, the black dragon stamina runs 24 turns in 4 hours and 6 turns in 1 hour, the 1d10 fatigue chance is 10 minus the rest number, the fatigued flying rate is two-thirds with the 100-yard same-turn landing bar, the thrown damage is exactly 3d10 plus 10 spanning 11 to 40, and the post-fatigue rest is three times the normal period at 18 turns.

consts.name: wftStrenuousRiskTurns
consts.comment: a character runs the risk of becoming fatigued whenever he engages in strenuous activity for more than four turns in succession

consts.name: wftAvoidRiskRestTurns
consts.comment: to avoid the risk of fatigue a character must rest for two consecutive turns after four turns of strenuous activity

consts.name: wftFirstConCheckTurns
consts.comment: if the character chooses not to rest, he must make a Constitution Check after exerting himself for six consecutive turns

consts.name: wftSuccessExtraTurns
consts.comment: a successful check indicates he can remain active for at least five more turns

consts.name: wftCheckStepReductionTurns
consts.comment: every time a check is successful, the time until the next required check is reduced by one turn

consts.name: wftCheckIntervalMinTurns
consts.comment: the shrinking check interval bottoms out at a minimum of one turn

consts.name: wftFatigueScoreDrop
consts.comment: all of the ability scores of a fatigued character except comeliness are lowered by 2 until he rests for two consecutive hours

consts.name: wftFatigueClearRestHours
consts.comment: the fatigue penalties remain in effect until the character rests for two consecutive hours

consts.name: wftExampleStrScore
consts.comment: the strength example: a character with 18 strength who becomes fatigued loses his +1 bonus on to-hit rolls and has his damage bonus reduced from +2 to +1

consts.name: wftExampleConScore
consts.comment: the constitution example: a fighter with 18 constitution who becomes fatigued immediately loses 2 hit points for each hit die he has, reflecting his temporary constitution of 16

consts.name: wftExampleWisScore
consts.comment: the wisdom example: a cleric with 14 wisdom who becomes fatigued loses both of his bonus 1st-level spells, his effective wisdom now 12

consts.name: wftFatigueAtkSavePenalty
consts.comment: in addition to the ability-score penalties, a fatigued character suffers a -2 penalty on all attack rolls (to hit and damage) and saving throws

consts.name: wftFatigueCheckEveryTurns
consts.comment: a fatigued character continuing strenuous activity must make a Constitution Check once per turn, using his fatigue-reduced constitution score

consts.name: wftExhaustExtraScoreDrop
consts.comment: an exhausted character takes an additional -2 penalty on all of his ability scores, attack rolls and saving throws

consts.name: wftExhaustRecoverRestHours
consts.comment: if an exhausted character rests for one hour without interruption, he can recover from exhaustion by making a successful Constitution Check with his temporarily reduced score

consts.name: wftFatigueAfterExhaustRestHours
consts.comment: a character who recovers from exhaustion is only fatigued, and then recovers from fatigue by resting for another two hours

consts.name: wftAnimalNoFoodDays
consts.comment: an animal becomes fatigued if forced to go for two consecutive days without any food and water

consts.name: wftAnimalShortRationDays
consts.comment: an animal becomes fatigued if forced to subsist on less than its full normal daily ration for more than three consecutive days

consts.name: wftRationRecoveryRestHours
consts.comment: to recover from fatigue due to lack of nourishment, an animal must be given a full normal ration of food and water and allowed to rest for eight hours afterward

consts.name: wftOverworkBaseRestHours
consts.comment: to recover from fatigue due to overexertion, an animal must rest for 12 hours plus two hours for every hour it was overworked

consts.name: wftOverworkRestPerHour
consts.comment: the overwork recovery adds two hours of rest per hour of overwork

consts.name: wftHorseExampleOverworkHours
consts.comment: the horse example: pushed three hours beyond the normal limit of its stamina

consts.name: wftHorseExampleRestHours
consts.comment: the horse example: it remains fatigued until allowed to rest for at least 18 hours without interruption (12 + 2 per overworked hour)

consts.name: wftAnimalFatigueMoveNum
consts.comment: a fatigued animal moves at one-half of its normal movement rate - the numerator

consts.name: wftAnimalFatigueMoveDen
consts.comment: the fatigued animal movement fraction - the denominator

consts.name: wftBurstFullRateRoundsPerTurn
consts.comment: a fatigued animal is capable of occasional bursts of speed enabling it to move at its full normal rate for one round per turn

consts.name: wftFatiguedTerrainBarInches
consts.comment: a fatigued animal is not able to negotiate any terrain in which its full normal movement rate is 3 inches

consts.name: wftAnimalFatigueAcPlaces
consts.comment: the armor class of a fatigued animal is two places worse than normal, accounting for its slower reflexes

consts.name: wftAnimalFatigueAcFrom
consts.comment: the fatigued armor class example - the normal class

consts.name: wftAnimalFatigueAcTo
consts.comment: the fatigued armor class example - the worsened class

consts.name: wftExhaustionHourChancePct
consts.comment: if a fatigued animal is forced to keep working or moving, there is a 20 percent chance per hour, cumulative, that it will become exhausted

consts.name: wftExhaustionResetRestHours
consts.comment: after any rest period of at least one hour the cumulative chance of exhaustion begins again at 20 percent

consts.name: wftCollapseUnburdenedPct
consts.comment: an exhausted animal may collapse: 25 percent chance if unburdened

consts.name: wftCollapseBurdenedPct
consts.comment: the collapse chance if carrying a rider or a normal load: 50 percent

consts.name: wftCollapseOverloadedPct
consts.comment: the collapse chance if carrying more than a normal load: 75 percent

consts.name: wftExhaustDeathChancePct
consts.comment: there is a flat 50 percent chance that an animal driven to exhaustion will die within 1d4 hours, checked as soon as it collapses

consts.name: wftExhaustDeathWindowDie
consts.comment: the death window: the animal may die within 1d4 hours of collapse

consts.name: wftTraumaDie
consts.comment: once per hour for eight consecutive hours the Dungeon Master rolls 1d6 for the collapsed animal

consts.name: wftTraumaSubtract
consts.comment: the trauma roll subtracts 3 from the 1d6 result

consts.name: wftTraumaMaxLoss
consts.comment: the trauma roll yields a number in the range 0-3, the hit points lost during that hour

consts.name: wftTraumaHours
consts.comment: the trauma rolls run once per hour for eight consecutive hours - the critical period

consts.name: wftTraumaRegainPerHour
consts.comment: an animal that survives the critical period regains its lost hit points at the rate of 2 per hour

consts.name: wftDragonSafeTurns
consts.comment: the black dragon example: stamina values 24/6, safe flying time 24 consecutive turns

consts.name: wftDragonRestTurns
consts.comment: the black dragon rest value: 6 turns of landed rest to regain stamina

consts.name: wftDragonSafeHours
consts.comment: the black dragon safe flying time in hours: 24 turns is four hours

consts.name: wftDragonRestHours
consts.comment: the black dragon rest period in hours: 6 turns is one hour

consts.name: wftFatigueCheckDie
consts.comment: past the safe flying time the Dungeon Master rolls 1d10 on a turn-by-turn basis to see if the flying mount becomes fatigued

consts.name: wftFatigueChanceBase
consts.comment: the chance of fatigue is equal to 10 minus the second number of the stamina value

consts.name: wftDragonFatigueRollLow
consts.comment: the black dragon fatigues on any turn past its safe time when the 1d10 roll is 1-4 - the low end

consts.name: wftDragonFatigueRollHigh
consts.comment: the black dragon fatigue roll high end: 1-4 on 1d10 (10 minus its rest value of 6)

consts.name: wftExampleWindowTurns
consts.comment: the non-block example: over a period of 30 turns the dragon is aloft 24 and rests 6, within the safe limit

consts.name: wftExampleLastFlightTurns
consts.comment: the example variant: a 7-turn last flight period puts the dragon aloft 25 turns without 6 turns of rest, risking fatigue on the 7th turn

consts.name: wftFatigueMoveNum
consts.comment: on the turn fatigue sets in the flying mount movement rate drops to two-thirds of full normal - the numerator

consts.name: wftFatigueMoveDen
consts.comment: the fatigued flying mount movement fraction - the denominator

consts.name: wftFatigueLossPerRoundYards
consts.comment: a fatigued flying mount gradually loses altitude at 10 yards per round

consts.name: wftSameTurnLandingAltitudeYards
consts.comment: a flying mount not more than 100 yards above the ground and not forced to remain aloft can descend and make a safe landing in the same turn fatigue sets in

consts.name: wftBuffetDieSides
consts.comment: for every 10 yards dived a rider suffers 1d2 hit points of damage at the end of the flight

consts.name: wftBuffetPerYards
consts.comment: the buffet damage accrues per 10 yards of dive distance

consts.name: wftThrownDmgMin
consts.comment: an unstrapped rider thrown on landing suffers 11-40 hit points of damage - the minimum

consts.name: wftThrownDmgMax
consts.comment: the thrown-rider damage maximum: 40

consts.name: wftThrownDiceCount
consts.comment: the thrown-rider damage is 3d10 plus 10

consts.name: wftThrownDieSides
consts.comment: the thrown-rider damage die: 3d10

consts.name: wftThrownBase
consts.comment: the thrown-rider damage base: +10 on 3d10

consts.name: wftPostFatigueRestMult
consts.comment: a fatigued flying mount that lands refuses to take off again for at least three times its normal rest period

consts.name: wftDragonPostFatigueRestTurns
consts.comment: the black dragon post-fatigue rest: 18 turns (three times its 6-turn rest period)

bools.name: wftOpenerThreat
bools.comment: even the strongest and hardiest characters and creatures cannot exert themselves indefinitely without becoming tired and needing rest; a long journey pressed too hard may exhaust the party long before the destination, and taking measures to avoid fatigue and exhaustion is not difficult and usually not inconvenient

bools.name: wftGroundDeathProficientLeap
bools.comment: the R488 cut tail: if the flying mount dies close to the ground, the Dungeon Master may allow a character with proficiency in riding the mount to leap from its back and land safely on the ground

bools.name: wftStrenuousOverfullMove
bools.comment: a character moving at greater than his full normal movement rate is engaged in strenuous activity

bools.name: wftStrenuousMelee
bools.comment: a character involved in melee combat is engaged in strenuous activity

bools.name: wftStrenuousOtherExamples
bools.comment: continuous climbing, swimming against a strong current, and moving while severely encumbered are other examples of strenuous activity

bools.name: wftCheckFailFatigued
bools.comment: failure on the Constitution Check indicates the character is fatigued

bools.name: wftIntervalShrinksPerSuccess
bools.comment: each successful check grants activity but shortens the interval to the next required check, to a minimum of one turn

bools.name: wftHighConEventuallyCaught
bools.comment: a character with an extremely high constitution may keep performing a strenuous activity for several hours, but the odds will eventually catch up with him

bools.name: wftFatigueScoresExceptComeliness
bools.comment: all of the ability scores of a fatigued character except comeliness are lowered by 2, and most incidental benefits bestowed by the higher scores are also lost as long as he remains fatigued

bools.name: wftStr18ExampleDetail
bools.comment: the 18-strength fatigued example: the +1 to-hit bonus is lost and the damage bonus drops from +2 to +1, among other penalties

bools.name: wftCon18ExampleDetail
bools.comment: the 18-constitution fatigued example: the fighter loses 2 hit points for each hit die, his actual temporary constitution score being only 16

bools.name: wftWis14ExampleDetail
bools.comment: the 14-wisdom fatigued example: the cleric loses both bonus 1st-level spells; if spells are in memory two 1st-level spells are lost at random, higher-level spells lost instead if fewer than two are held, the bonus spells cannot be regained, and every spell cast carries a chance of failure until he is no longer fatigued

bools.name: wftChecksUseReducedScores
bools.comment: any Proficiency Check or Ability Check required of a fatigued character has a smaller chance of success, the die roll compared to the current ability score instead of the normal score

bools.name: wftFatiguedCanContinue
bools.comment: a fatigued character can continue to perform strenuous activity, but must make a Constitution Check once per turn while doing so

bools.name: wftFatiguedFailExhausted
bools.comment: if a fatigued character fails a Constitution Check, he becomes exhausted

bools.name: wftExhaustedOnlyDefense
bools.comment: an exhausted character can attempt to defend himself or perform some other physical action only when failure to move would mean risking death

bools.name: wftExhaustedCannotAct
bools.comment: otherwise an exhausted character is not capable of any voluntary physical activity: he cannot move under his own power, put on or take off armor, build a fire, or do anything else requiring minimal strength and muscle control

bools.name: wftExhaustRecoverByCheck
bools.comment: one hour of uninterrupted rest plus a successful Constitution Check (at the reduced score) leaves the character only fatigued instead of exhausted

bools.name: wftExhaustRecoverFailLoop
bools.comment: if the recovery check fails, the character remains exhausted and must rest for another hour before trying again

bools.name: wftRestWhileCarried
bools.comment: a fatigued or exhausted character can rest while being carried, as long as no strength or balance is needed to remain in position and he is not bounced or jostled; a fighter draping a frail magic-user across his shoulders works, but a choppy or zig-zagging path across rugged or very rugged terrain spoils the rest

bools.name: wftRestTiedToMount
bools.comment: an exhausted character can rest while securely tied to the back of a horse or other mount, but only if the mount moves easily (no faster than normal movement rate) over terrain that is not difficult for the animal to negotiate

bools.name: wftAnimalCrossRefs
bools.comment: the stamina process is in the Encumbrance and Movement section, the animal-care specifics are in Mounts and Beasts of Burden, and these general fatigue rules apply in all cases not specifically accounted for elsewhere

bools.name: wftAnimalFatiguedNoFood
bools.comment: two consecutive days without any food and water fatigues the animal

bools.name: wftAnimalFatiguedShortRation
bools.comment: less than the full normal daily ration for more than three consecutive days fatigues the animal

bools.name: wftRationRecoveryNeedsBoth
bools.comment: nourishment recovery requires BOTH the full ration and the full eight hours of rest; missing either leaves the animal fatigued

bools.name: wftOverworkRecoveryFormula
bools.comment: overwork recovery is 12 hours of rest plus two hours per hour overworked; the pushed horse example rests 18 hours

bools.name: wftFatiguedHalfMoveWithBursts
bools.comment: a fatigued animal moves at half its normal rate with occasional one-round-per-turn bursts of full speed

bools.name: wftFatiguedTerrainBarDetail
bools.comment: the fatigued terrain bar: no terrain whose full normal rate is 3 inches; a fatigued horse cannot move in very rugged terrain carrying more than a normal load, and a fatigued camel cannot move in very rugged terrain under any circumstances

bools.name: wftFatiguedAcWorse
bools.comment: a fatigued animal is two armor class places worse (7 to 9, for instance) - slower reflexes

bools.name: wftExcitedOnlyHandlerCalms
bools.comment: if a fatigued animal becomes excited, only a character with proficiency in animal handling can get it to calm down, and that chance is only as great as the normal chance for a nonproficient character

bools.name: wftWorkedFatiguedExhaustionChance
bools.comment: a fatigued animal forced to keep working faces a cumulative 20 percent chance per hour of becoming exhausted

bools.name: wftBriefWorkRestResets
bools.comment: worked briefly without exhaustion and then rested at least an hour, the animal recovers somewhat and the cumulative chance starts again at 20 percent

bools.name: wftExhaustedStopsInTracks
bools.comment: an exhausted animal stops in its tracks, incapable of moving or working; near death, its survival without magical aid depends entirely on chance

bools.name: wftExhaustedCollapseOblivious
bools.comment: the exhausted animal may collapse (25/50/75 percent by burden) and while incapacitated is oblivious to anything going on around it

bools.name: wftExhaustedNoPanicNoDefense
bools.comment: an exhausted animal will not become excited or panicked even if threatened by fire, but will make no attempt to protect itself from attack or injury

bools.name: wftExhaustedDeathCheck
bools.comment: a flat 50 percent chance that the exhausted animal dies within 1d4 hours, checked by the Dungeon Master as soon as it collapses

bools.name: wftExhaustedTraumaDrain
bools.comment: once per hour for eight consecutive hours the trauma roll is 1d6 minus 3, losing 0-3 hit points per hour; at a hit-point total of 0 the animal is dead

bools.name: wftExhaustedTraumaRecovery
bools.comment: surviving the eight-hour critical period, the animal regains lost hit points at 2 per hour and is recovered from exhaustion (but still fatigued) when the total reaches its pre-exhaustion level

bools.name: wftFlyingNeverExhausted
bools.comment: a flying mount can never become exhausted; but if it becomes fatigued, the rider stands to suffer at least as much as the animal, and perhaps a whole lot more

bools.name: wftStaminaTableCrossRef
bools.comment: the Characteristics of Flying Mounts table in the Movement and Encumbrance section gives the stamina values; the first number is the safe flying time

bools.name: wftHeavyLoadReducesSafe
bools.comment: the safe flying time may be reduced if the creature is heavily loaded down

bools.name: wftFatigueRollPastSafe
bools.comment: once aloft for consecutive turns equal to its safe flying time, the Dungeon Master begins rolling 1d10 each turn thereafter

bools.name: wftFatigueChanceFormula
bools.comment: the chance of fatigue is equal to 10 minus the second number of the stamina value

bools.name: wftDragonExample
bools.comment: the black dragon 24/6: ridden through the air 24 consecutive turns (four hours) without risk, then it must land and rest (not fly) 6 turns (one hour) to regain stamina; past the 24th turn it fatigues on a 1d10 roll of 1-4

bools.name: wftFlyingRestNotFullBlocks
bools.comment: flying time and rest time need not be taken in full blocks: flown 12, rested 3, flown 6, rested 2, flown 6, rested 1 - 24 aloft and 6 rest in a 30-turn window is safe; but the 7-turn last flight means 25 turns aloft without the 6 turns of rest, risking fatigue

bools.name: wftExceedNeedsFullRest
bools.comment: a creature that exceeds its safe flying time and is brought to a safe landing must have a FULL rest period or it is subject to fatigue as soon as it takes to the air again

bools.name: wftTrackAloftAndRest
bools.comment: keep careful track of how much the mount has flown and rested; exceeding the safe flying time by even a small amount can cause an extended delay on a long-distance journey

bools.name: wftFatigueTwoThirdsMove
bools.comment: on the turn fatigue sets in the movement rate drops to two-thirds of normal and the mount begins losing altitude at 10 yards per round

bools.name: wftFatigueSafeLandingSameTurn
bools.comment: not more than 100 yards up and not forced to remain aloft, the fatigued mount can descend and land safely in the same turn

bools.name: wftSecondTurnSteepDive
bools.comment: more than 100 yards up when fatigue sets in, the mount is still aloft when its second turn of fatigue begins: it stops descending gradually and goes into a steep dive toward a resting place; riders face an increased chance of falling and the sudden stop at the end

bools.name: wftDiveBuffetDamage
bools.comment: for every 10 yards dived before reaching the ground a rider suffers 1d2 hit points at the end of the flight from the buffeting of the crash, bounce or skid to a stop

bools.name: wftBuffetHalvedFor
bools.comment: the buffet damage is halved for a character with proficiency in airborne riding or one securely strapped (upper and lower body) to the back of the mount

bools.name: wftUnstrappedThrown
bools.comment: a rider without at least his lower body strapped suffers no buffeting damage but is thrown from the mount when it lands, suffering 11-40 hit points (3d10 + 10) from the abrasion and impact of the tumble

bools.name: wftPostFatigueGroundRefusal
bools.comment: a fatigued flying mount that lands refuses to take off again for at least three times its normal rest period (18 turns for a black dragon), unless self-preservation dictates that it become airborne

bools.name: wftEarlyTakeoffFatigueRisk
bools.comment: taking off again for any reason before the full post-fatigue rest period expires, the mount has a chance of becoming fatigued on every turn it remains aloft

examples.note: the strenuous rhythm: risk after more than 4 turns, 2 turns of rest avoids it, the first Constitution Check at 6 turns, 5 more turns on success, the interval shrinking by 1 to a minimum of 1
examples.expr: m['wftStrenuousRiskTurns']() != 4 or m['wftAvoidRiskRestTurns']() != 2 or m['wftFirstConCheckTurns']() != 6 or m['wftSuccessExtraTurns']() != 5 or m['wftCheckStepReductionTurns']() != m['wftCheckIntervalMinTurns']()

examples.note: the fatigue penalties: the score drop 2, the exhausted extra drop equal to it, the attack/save penalty equal to it, and the 2-hour clear equal to the post-exhaustion fatigue clear
examples.expr: m['wftFatigueScoreDrop']() != 2 or m['wftExhaustExtraScoreDrop']() != m['wftFatigueScoreDrop']() or m['wftFatigueAtkSavePenalty']() != m['wftFatigueScoreDrop']() or m['wftFatigueClearRestHours']() != m['wftFatigueAfterExhaustRestHours']()

examples.note: the example scores: strength 18, constitution 18, wisdom 14
the recovery rhythm: the fatigued check once per turn and the exhausted recovery rest of 1 hour
the animal nourishment rules: 2 days without food and water, 3 days short rations, 8 hours rest to recover
the overwork formula: 12 hours plus 2 per overworked hour, the 3-hour horse needing 18 hours of rest
the fatigued animal effects: half movement, the 3-inch terrain bar, and the armor class example 7 to 9 being exactly 2 places
examples.expr: m['wftAnimalFatigueMoveNum']() * 2 != m['wftAnimalFatigueMoveDen']() or m['wftFatiguedTerrainBarInches']() != 3 or m['wftAnimalFatigueAcTo']() - m['wftAnimalFatigueAcFrom']() != m['wftAnimalFatigueAcPlaces']()

examples.note: the exhaustion chance: 20 percent per hour cumulative, resetting after a rest of at least 1 hour
the collapse ladder: 25 unburdened, 50 with a rider or normal load, 75 overloaded, in equal 25-point steps
the trauma rules: 1d6 minus 3 yields 0-3, the floor at zero, the 8-hour critical period and the 2-per-hour regain
